correctness.rationale: The full kernel follows exactly from three mutually orthogonal centered trigonometric generators and normalized area. The limiting Legendre kernel has sharp endpoint norm 1+12 sqrt(6)/25: a direct Cauchy--Schwarz margin covers |x|<=21/25; a strictly positive factored derivative covers 21/25<=|x|<=1. Uniform analytic convergence and simple-root continuation preserve both global maximizers for small h. Taylor expansion of the exact Gram kernel and exact negative-root integration give -387 sqrt(6)/21875 as the quadratic coefficient, with O(h^4) from even analytic dependence. The packaged script repeats exact symbolic identities and 25 finite checks; finite examples are corroboration only. Largest admissible aperture is not proved.

originality.rationale: The central claim is the sharp global endpoint projection norm for fixed three trigonometric modes in the small-aperture regime, including strict endpoint localization and exact negative second-order defect. Full relevant sections of pre-2016 Fourier-extension stability work and the 2018 prolate-kernel/Lebesgue-function analysis were compared; the inspected results concern polynomial equivalences, Gram-condition growth and increasing bandwidth at fixed extension scale. None of the examined statements determines the optimized fixed-bandwidth small-aperture second coefficient without new sign-root and extremizer arguments. This is qualified by residual priority risk and is not an independent novelty certificate.
residual_risks: A degree-one Fourier-extension Lebesgue-constant computation may be available in prior literature under a different name; a prior kernel identity alone is not evidence that the exact optimized correction was previously evaluated.
The 2018 prolate-kernel result applies to the same family and could facilitate rediscovery of the coefficient; full historical priority beyond inspected passages and searches remains uncertain.

The primary classification 41A10 treats the norm as an approximation-theory stability invariant; neighboring Fourier-analysis classifications exist, but this claim concerns the sharp least-squares approximation projector norm, not Fourier coefficient summability.

value.rationale: The three-mode continuous Fourier extension is the natural first nontrivial example of least-squares approximation by trigonometric functions beyond a physical interval. Its coefficient Gram condition degenerates as the arc collapses, but its function-space operator norm tends to a finite sharp Legendre constant. The exact negative second-order coefficient supplies a first quantitative curvature correction, while eventual extremizer uniqueness is necessary for sharp global sensitivity, distinguishing this from an arbitrary Taylor expansion of a pointwise kernel.
